intended_object: The subring of R⟦X⟧ made of the c-restricted power series, i.e. the series ∑ aₙXⁿ with ‖aₙ‖·cⁿ → 0, over an ultrametric normed ring R. For c = 1 this is the Tate algebra R⟨X⟩. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition specializes `MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring` to one variable (σ = Unit) with the constant weight `fun _ ↦ c`. Its carrier is `{f | IsRestricted c f}`. By `isRestricted_iff'` in the same file, this condition is equivalent to ‖coeff n f‖·cⁿ → 0 as n → ∞, which is the textbook condition.

The ultrametric hypothesis is needed. Without it the set is not closed under multiplication: over ℝ with c = 1, take aₙ = 1/√n. Then aₙ → 0, but the coefficients of the Cauchy product, ∑ₖ 1/√(k(n−k)), tend to π rather than to 0. The assumption `NormedRing R` is the natural generality: commutativity is not used.

This is the univariate counterpart of the general multivariate definition. Mathlib keeps separate univariate APIs on `PowerSeries` alongside `MvPowerSeries`, so delegating to the general definition is not too narrow.
